text: By 2030, reduce biodiversity loss and maintain ecological integrity by including all territory in spatial planning and ensuring effective management.
activities:
1.1. Conduct Red List of Ecosystems assessments
1.2.  Maintain the proportion of natural ecosystems and prevent further decline
1.3. Integrate biodiversity considerations into general land-use plans and soum territorial development plans to reduce biodiversity loss, and systematically reflect rare fauna, flora, and their habitats in these planning documents

text: By 2030, restore at least 30 percent of degraded ecosystems and improve ecological integrity and connectivity.
By 2030, 30% of the country's total area will be included in the special protected area network, representing major ecosystem types and strengthening ecological connectivity.
By 2030, Reduce the risk of extinction of threatened species and conserve genetic diversity
activities:
4.1. Conduct baseline surveys on distribution and abundance

4.4. Strengthen the legal framework for biodiversity conservation, sustainable use and reducing biodiversity loss

text: By 2030, register, control, and assess the impacts of invasive alien species, while building the capacity to combat and prevent their adverse effects.
activities:

5.2. Undertake research and establish a registry/database on alien species

text: By 2030, reduce pollution from all sources to levels that are not harmful to biodiversity and ecosystem functions and human health.
activities:
6.1. Promote sound pesticide use, establish a pesticide tracking system, and introduce alternatives to chemical pesticides
6.2. Identify soil contaminated by pesticide residues and strengthen laboratory capacity to determine soil pesticide residues
6.3. Remediate soil contaminated by pesticides
6.4. Adopt international IPSM standards
6.5. Improve economic instruments for waste management and establish legal provisions based on extended producer responsibility and the polluter-pays principle
6.6. Establish temporary hazardous waste storage facilities
6.7. Translate and approve ISO standards on micro- and macroplastics in the environment
6.8. Prohibit import and use in Mongolia of chemicals newly added to Annex III of the Rotterdam Convention

text: By 2030, minimize the impact of climate change on biodiversity and increase its resilience through mitigation, adaptation, and disaster risk reduction actions through nature-based solution and ecosystem-based approaches.
activities:
7.1. Conduct and expand long-term monitoring and establish monitoring points for climate change
7.2. Increase carbon sequestration by expanding forest cover
7.3. Strengthen risk assessment, early warning systems and local preparedness under the Sendai Framework, and integrate nature-based solutions into disaster risk management to reduce climate-related disaster risks

text: By 2030, reduce ecosystem degradation by supporting the development of sustainable, highly productive forestry and agriculture, while introducing nature-based practices.

8.7. Reduce chemical plant protection inputs by promoting mixed cropping
8.8. Establish shelterbelts on cropland
8.9. Identify agricultural lands negatively affecting biodiversity
8.10. Diversify and develop model forestry/agroforestry

text: By 2030, increase the benefits of nature to people through ecosystem services derived from nature-based solutions.
activities:
9.1. Use ecosystem services valuation in policy, land use and sector planning to restore nature’s benefits in real terms
9.2. Reduce sources of air pollution
9.3. Improve air quality monitoring
9.4. Increase secure sources of drinking water for the population and promote efficient use

text: By 2030, increase the area of urban green and blue infrastructure.
activities:

10.2. Increase per capita urban green space to international benchmarks
10.3. Organize citizen-based tree planting and maintenance campaigns
10.4. Create artificial lakes and water features
10.5. Integrate green/blue infrastructure into urban master plans and partial development plans
10.6. Establish new urban forests, parks and green spaces

text: By 2030, develop a comprehensive database for genetic resources and traditional knowledge, while strengthening legal and governance frameworks to ensure the fair and equitable sharing of benefits.
activities:
11.1. Create the legal framework for benefit-sharing from the utilization of genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge

11.5. Establish a seed bank for wild plants

text: By 2030, Integrate biodiversity issues into the policies and planning of all sectors.

text: By 2030, establish systems to monitor and transparently report the impacts, risks, and outcomes of business activities regarding biodiversity.

text: By 2030, minimize overconsumption and waste through supporting public education on sustainable consumption.
activities:

14.3. Promote zero waste and circular economy values through traditional nomadic culture and nature-friendly practices
14.4. Support sustainable consumption initiatives to reduce food waste
14.5. Promote household and institutional practices for water and energy saving and greywater reuse

text: By 2030, enhance the legislative, governance, and monitoring systems for genetically modified organisms.

text: By 2030, reform subsidies and incentives that have negative impacts on biodiversity, while increasing environmentally positive (green) incentives.

text: Substantially and progressively increase financial resources towards biodiversity conservation from all sources, in an effective, timely, innovative and easily accessible manner.
activities:
17.1. Increase private sector financing for biodiversity within biodiversity finance systems and environmental and social responsibility frameworks
17.2. Raise public expenditure on the environment sector to internationally comparable levels as a share of GDP
17.3. Adopt the revised Law on Natural Resource Use Fees and strengthen implementation

text: Strengthen capacity-building and development, access to and transfer of technology, and promote development of and access to innovation and technical and scientific cooperation in biodiversity conservation.

text: By 2030, data and information relevant to biodiversity and ecosystem services are widely accessible to decision makers, scientists and the public to guide effective and equitable governance, integrated and participatory management of biodiversity.
activities:

19.3. Promote nature-based solutions and green technologies through multi-stakeholder outreach and encourage active participation

text: By 2030, ensure full, equitable, inclusive, effective, and gender-responsive representation and participation in decision-making and implementation related to biodiversity and ensure rights over relevant resources of local communities, women and girls as well as youth.
activities:

text: Improve the policy, legal, structural, and organizational environment for the climate change adaptation of the sector.
actions:
Measures:
1. Revising irrigation regimes and water use norms for pastures, agriculture, forests,
industry, and mining to increase recycling and introduce water-efficient technologies.
Establish a permanent monitoring system for water use,
2. Determining ecological flows and sustainable abstraction levels through hydrological and
biological studies to guide rational water management,
3. Updating flood runoff standards and implementing structural standards for protective
infrastructure and flow capacity assessments.

text: Enhance the resilience of the water sector through the utilization of advanced technologies for conservation, restoration, sustainable use and secure water availability.
actions:
Measures:
1. Including river headwater sources under special protection,
2. Expanding medium-scale hydrogeological mapping to assess water resources,
3. Increasing monitoring of groundwater wells, improving databases and reporting
mechanisms,
4. Creating water accumulation facilities and ponds in humid and sub-humid zones,
5. Supporting national satellite technology to monitor glaciers, lakes, and reservoirs, and
automating hydrological data transmission and acquisition,
6. Regulating the thermal regime of water through riparian forestation and monitoring its
effectiveness,
7. Restoring and expanding surface–groundwater interaction monitoring networks and
water balance assessment systems,
8. Implement projects in arid and semi-arid regions through partnerships between local
governments, the private sector, the mining industry, and light and heavy industry to
establish Managed Aquifer Recharge (MAR) systems, covered reservoirs, and infiltration
wells for the replenishment of groundwater resources,
9. In cool and moderately humid zones, construct irrigation ponds for hay and crop
cultivation, fish and aquatic species breeding ponds, and community ponds (ardyn khuv).
Develop natural overflow systems (khalia-toshin) and, through canals and pipelines,
deliver water to wildlife and livestock in semi-arid and arid areas to improve water access,
10. Support pasture irrigation and household water use by delivering water to drying
endorheic lakes, enabling the cultivation of berries, vegetables, and household-level fish
farming,
11. Regulate the thermal regime of river and lake waters through shading from riparian
forests, implement ecosystem protection measures, and support the breeding of native
fish species such as taimen (Hucho taimen), lenok (Brachymystax), Arctic
grayling (Thymallus arcticus), and other indigenous aquatic species.
Conditional measures:
12. Retaining the projected 6.4 km³ of meltwater in upstream basins of rivers such as Khovd
(Altangadas, Bukhmurun), Bulgan, Kharkhiraa, Turgun, Zuil, Khushoot, Namir, Bayan, and
Gorkhon,
13. Developing feasibility studies (FS) for Orkhon-Gobi and Shuren Hydropower Plants (HPPs)
for hydropower generation and flow transfer from the Selenge and Orkhon River Basins
to Gobi region,
14. Establish water accumulation zones in low-evaporation areas such as the upper and
middle reaches of the Baidrag, Ongi, Taats, Ar-Aguit, and Tuin river basins, and address
water supply issues along these rivers. At the same time, restore and protect ecosystems
of Ulaan, Orog, Taatsiin Tsagaan, and Khaya lakes and associated wetlands, while
developing infrastructure and capacity to regulate lake water regimes.

text: Strengthen early warning systems and reduce disaster risks at all levels.

text: Reduce pasture pressure by raising young livestock using advanced methods and technologies, developing biosecure compartment farming and supplying meat to target markets.
actions:
Measures:
1. Support private sector initiatives to raise young livestock using advanced methods and
technologies for meat production,
2. Develop protected farms aimed at preparing meat for target markets and implement
traceability technology,
3. Develop and implement response strategies for new and re-emerging livestock and
animal infectious diseases.
Conditional measure:
4. Provide financial and land support to farmers engaged in intensive young livestock

text: Improve livestock water and feed supply, quality and management to strengthen resilience against natural risks.

Measures:

protection management,
2. Develop small-scale water collection facilities such as reservoirs, ponds, and pools
utilizing excess snow and rainwater,

initiatives to grow fodder crops in winter-spring camps,

Conditional measure:
6. Develop wholesale trade and warehouse operations through herders' cooperatives in
provinces and soums where hay and feed preparation is not possible.

for livestock production and pasture utilization.
Conditional measures:
4. Strengthen technical and technological capacity for remote sensing monitoring of
pasture conditions,
5. Train specialists and implement international projects in smart technologies for livestock
production and pasture utilization.

text: Establish sustainable and rational collaborative management practices for pastures and expand the scope of pasture restoration.

5. Introduce and expand the scope of pasture restoration technologies and innovations.

text: The agricultural sector will reduce 5.277 million tons of CO2 until 2030 and 9.78 million tons of CO2 until 2035 by adhering (national livestock herd to 50 million head) ecological carrying capacity of rangelands and improving livestock economic turnover through increasing export and meat supply to the domestic.
By improving the circulation of livestock and livestock raw materials and increasing exports, Livestock CO2 emissions shall be reduced by 4.15 million tons by 2030 and 7.48 million tons by 2035.
By increasing meat supply to the domestic market will reduce livestock CO2 emissions by 1.12 million tons by 2030 and by 2.29 million tons by 2035

Reduce Soil Organic Carbon loss by restoring 10% of heavily degraded rangelands within the forest-steppe (3%) and steppe (7%) ecological zones, moving land from Recovery Class IV (heavily degraded) to Recovery Class III (moderately degraded).

Ensure the inclusion of all social groups—including men, women, persons with disabilities, vulnerable communities, youth, and the elderly—in climate actions, while adhering to the core principles of gender-responsive climate budgeting
actions:
Promote the full, equal and meaningful participation of diverse social groups - women, youth and differently abled people- at all levels of climate-related decision-making processes
Strengthen the skills of relevant decision-makers/officials in gender-responsive climate budgeting and allocate dedicated funding to support gender-inclusive climate initiatives that promote gender equality and women’s empowerment
Establish mechanisms to collect sex-disaggregated data and develop national gender and climate change indicators and tools across all levels of climate action implementation to support evidence-based and inclusive policymaking

text: Ensure that all climate change mitigation and adaptation actions are gender-responsive by explicitly respecting, promoting, and considering gender equality and the empowerment of women, in line with the Paris Agreement, particularly Article 7.5 on gender-responsive adaptation.

Provide capacity development training for policymakers, planners, and implementers on gender-responsive climate action
Support women's leadership and capacity in climate-related sectors, especially in local and vulnerable communities

text: Establish a regionally differentiated land payment system and limit livestock numbers to match pasture carrying capacity, balancing grazing pressure across ecological zones.
activities:
Introduce Responsible Nomad good practice standards (MNS 6891:2020) and conduct compliance certification
Implement livestock head tax legislation to incentivize herd size management
Develop provincial pasture use and protection rules
Train herders in carrying capacity-aligned grazing practices

text: Transform agriculture into an environmentally friendly, climate-change adapted, risk-resilient, socially responsive, responsible, highly productive, and sustainable leading economic sector.
activities:
Enact law on reducing adverse climate change effects on traditional livestock husbandry
Launch nationwide New Cooperative movement to strengthen herder livelihoods
Establish climate-adapted agricultural zones in central provinces
Develop green economy-oriented production and sustainable resource use across the sector

text: Strengthen capacity for climate adaptation and risk reduction in agriculture, improve agricultural insurance systems, and reduce economic losses from sudden climate-related disasters.
activities:
Improve indexed livestock insurance with revised loss thresholds and broader coverage
Develop crop insurance legislation
Provide restocking support for herders who lost 50% or more of livestock to climate disasters
Implement ECCO-FARM climate adaptation project across five provinces

text: Establish a clear legal framework for pasture use, improvement, and protection; create a unified pasture management system to reduce pasture degradation and desertification.
activities:
Pass Herder Primary Union legal status law enabling seasonal pasture contracts
Establish 4-season pasture use contract system for herder unions
Require herders to follow 3 packages of good practices including pasture management
Develop pasture management plans aligned with soum land-use plans

text: Set upper limits on livestock numbers, types, and composition aligned with ecology and pasture carrying capacity; combat pasture pests and rodents; and increase pasture, fodder, and water supply to reduce agricultural risks.
activities:
Conduct pasture pest control on 650,000 to 1,000,000 ha annually
Drill 100-200 deep wells and 400-500 simple wells annually for pasture water supply
Designate approximately 3 million ha of reserve pasture zones
Set annual overwintering livestock limits based on carrying capacity assessments
Produce and distribute improved fodder crop seeds

text: Develop green economy-oriented livestock husbandry that preserves traditional nomadic cultural heritage in rangelands while establishing intensified, technology-driven farming near urban areas, sustainably using resources.
activities:
Maintain traditional nomadic rangeland-based herding as the dominant pastoral system
Establish intensified meat and dairy farming zones near Darkhan-Uul, Selenge, and Tuv provinces
Direct cooperative investment loans toward 14 climate adaptation measures
Promote sustainable resource use through herder cooperatives

text: Develop smart technology-based agriculture to increase competitiveness and value of Mongolian crops grown in fertile soils, and increase agricultural exports.
activities:
Introduce precision agriculture and smart farming technologies
Improve soil fertility through fallow management and soil enrichment
Support crop seed quality improvement and certification
Expand export-oriented crop production

text: Expand irrigated agricultural production capacity by investing in modern irrigation infrastructure and bringing fallow lands into efficient cultivation.
activities:
Install modern irrigation equipment across agricultural enterprises
Bring fallow and abandoned cropland back into irrigated rotation
Replace traditional tillage with water-efficient agrotechnical methods
Improve fallow preparation using chemical and combined approaches

text: Promote cooperative initiatives, eco-initiatives, and investment in agriculture to increase sustainable resource utilization.
activities:
Establish herder cooperatives as primary units for sustainable resource management
Channel cooperative investment loans toward climate change adaptation activities
Promote eco-friendly and sustainable production practices through cooperative networks

text: Expand state specially protected areas to cover 30% of national territory by 2030, 33% by 2040, and 35% by 2050, ensuring representation of major ecosystem types and freshwater source areas.
activities:
Conduct studies to identify freshwater, forest, and biodiversity-important areas for protection
Expand the state specially protected areas network from 20.1% to 30% by 2030
Increase protected river source areas from 48.3% to 60% by 2030 and 75% by 2050
Increase protected forest area from 39.1% to 50% by 2030 and 60% by 2050

text: Increase forest cover to 9% of national territory through reforestation, supporting natural forest regeneration, and strengthening forest protection measures, thereby increasing carbon dioxide sequestration.
activities:
Conduct reforestation and afforestation programmes
Support natural forest regeneration and expansion
Strengthen forest protection against fire, illegal logging, and pest outbreaks
Establish forest agroparks to reduce direct harvesting pressure

text: Implement a national programme to protect soil, reduce land degradation, and combat desertification.
activities:
Protect soil fertility and moisture to prevent land degradation
Prevent and reverse desertification in affected zones
Restore degraded and contaminated land and return it to productive use
Develop smart environmental monitoring systems for land condition

text: Implement the Green Belt project to rehabilitate land degraded by mining, agriculture, infrastructure, and urban development, increasing user accountability and restoring land for productive reuse.
activities:
Rehabilitate land degraded by mining operations
Restore agricultural land damaged by overuse and erosion
Reclaim areas affected by infrastructure and urban development
Increase land user accountability for environmental restoration

text: Improve the regulatory framework for valuing ecosystem services, update ecological-economic assessments, and raise public awareness of ecosystem service values and benefits.
activities:
Develop and improve regulations for ecosystem service valuation
Update ecological-economic assessments of natural resources
Communicate ecosystem service values and benefits to the public
Integrate ecosystem service valuation into policy and planning decisions

text: Reduce subsidies to economic activities that negatively affect ecosystems and biodiversity, and support ecosystem conservation and protection activities.
activities:
Identify and assess subsidies that negatively impact ecosystems and biodiversity
Phase down harmful subsidies in agriculture, mining, and other sectors
Redirect financial support toward ecosystem conservation and protection
Develop science-based professional education for environmental conservation
